title: I Followed the Aviary Feeding Log Into the Bucket the Intern Pocketed

parts.text: I weighed diet 4 at 8:22 a.m. and intern Pell palmed mealworms from my labeled bucket. The sheet said: WEIGH THE DIET. LOG THE GRAMS. NO POCKETS. I was twenty-nine, volunteer, holding a gram card. Pell shrugged. "Interns are the birds." I photographed the sheet, the card, and the palm. Then I asked for the feeding log. At 8:28 the curator pinged why Pell's name was on missing grams. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The curator can see Pell's palm on diet 4 missing grams in the feeding log.

social.video_title: The intern palmed mealworms from my labeled bucket — Part 1/2
social.description: Aviary, a gram card, a pocketed diet. I logged the missing weight. Would you have asked the curator?

parts.text: Pell called it a treat until the curator asked for the still. I printed the log, the sheet, and the photo. The grams returned. Pell logged diets and told the next intern treats were always about optics. Optics is a word interns use when buckets exist. Feeding now has a second line: POCKETS ARE NOT DIETS. I keep diet 4. Pell brown-bags the jokes. The aviary finally looks like a sheet, not a snack. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Feeding log, returned grams, and a second line. Was a treat ever my bucket?
